title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of employers' organizations

description.narrative: Employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs) in China operate in a rapidly evolving environment shaped by industrial upgrading, the green transition, digitalisation, and the growing global engagement of Chinese enterprises. The China Enterprise Confederation (CEC) plays a central role in representing employersâ€™ interests at the national level. However, like many EBMOs worldwide, CEC faces significant capacity-related challenges. These include adapting organizational structures and services to meet changing member needs, strengthening strategic planning and knowledge management, and responding effectively to emerging policy and labour market issues. As a result, expectations of EBMOs are increasing, particularly in their ability to provide effective representation, policy input, and member services, while engaging constructively in social dialogue and international cooperation. EBMOs across Asia and the Pacific have accumulated valuable experience in navigating institutional reform, responding to economic and structural change, and strengthening internal systems, processes, and organizational structures to enhance the value delivered to their members. These experiences offer practical models and lessons that can inform CECâ€™s own institutional development. Regional dialogue and peer learning provide an opportunity for CEC to exchange experiences with other EBMOs, adapt relevant good practices, and strengthen its capacity in a manner that is context specific and demand driven. Expected results include: strengthened institutional and organizational capacity of CEC and its members through the adaptation of practical models and lessons learned shared by EBMO in the region.
